title: affordable-prefill-agent-and-quant-constrainer
author: Corey Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Customers want automated, low-risk defaults that reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) Affordable Prefill Agent - a runtime operator that enforces tenant-level prefill budgets and soft-clamps prefill sizes based on recent unit economics; (2) Quant Constrainer - a rollout-safe mechanism to attach quantization-matrix constraints to candidate model variants and to automatically fallback when quality regressions are detected.

Summary of changes: added runtime agent, new policy DSL fields, CLI controls for dry-run/apply, end-to-end integration tests, telemetry and perf benches, and documentation. This is intended to be a non-breaking opt-in feature but ships safe defaults.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement Affordable Prefill Agent with pluggable heuristics (LRU/decay)
- [x] Implement Quant Constrainer with staged rollout and metrics guardrails
- [x] Add CLI flags: --econ-dryrun, --econ-apply, --quant-constraint-file
- [x] Unit and integration tests for agent decision logic
- [x] Telemetry: econ.prefill.actions, econ.quant.fallbacks, econ.simulated_savings
- [x] Benchmark harness: microbench for latency impact, end-to-end cost sim
- [x] Docs: runtime.md section and console feature note

Why this is unique: Rather than replacing existing batching/autotune, the agent acts as a conservative, tenant-aware layer that suggests or enforces smaller prefill sizes during high-cost situations and coordinates with quant profile rollouts to keep regressions contained. It is designed for low-friction adoption (dry-run first, then apply) and emphasizes observability.

Risks and mitigations: the agent runs with a throttling budget and never forces quantized variants without a quality pass. We added telemetry and an automatic rollback window (configurable via policy) and integration smoke tests to catch regressions in CI.

Related: Linear/ENG-4821 (prefill policy extension), ENG-4918 (quant rollout guardrails).

review_comments: Asha Patel: Please add a short-circuit flag so the agent can be turned off at runtime without redeploying. I see you have a config value but a runtime toggle would help incident response.
Corey Nguyen: Added --econ-disable-runtime flag and expose health endpoint that returns agent.enabled; updated README. (see commit a1c3f5b -> f6a1b44)
Mateo Rivera: How is correctness verified for quant fallback? Where are the evaluation thresholds coming from?

Corey Nguyen: Quant Constrainer reads quality thresholds from policy.quant_constraints.thresholds (defaults summarized in docs). We added a small evaluation harness in infra/ci to run the fallback on a sampled prompt set and included nightlies for further validation.

Corey Nguyen: Fixed by stubbing external telemetry and adding retry + timeout in integration job; re-ran CI.
